body.x: Lighters Company (CEO Hami Kim) announced its participation in CES 2025, which will be held in Las Vegas from January 7 to 10, as part of the K-Startup Pavilion.

Lighters Company operates the global K-pop fandom platform Kooky, which is dedicated to creating a fan-driven entertainment ecosystem. Unlike traditional platforms that primarily deliver artist-generated content, Kooky emphasizes fan participation through promotional activities and interactive events, empowering fans to support their favorite artists actively.

This unique approach has enabled Kooky to attract over 2 million users worldwide, establishing itself as a central hub for global K-pop fandom. Building a demand-driven fan platform aligns with the growing trend of fan-generated online and offline content, receiving positive recognition for its effectiveness.

At CES 2025, Lighters Company will showcase Kooky’s innovative technology, which leverages extensive fandom data. The platform analyzes artist popularity across demographics and regions, using these insights to connect and host fan events and localized promotions.

For instance, Kooky helps expand fan-initiated artist birthday celebrations into broader community-supported campaigns or facilitates fan meetings in target regions identified by artists. These efforts demonstrate the platform’s role in amplifying fan-driven initiatives and connecting artists with local audiences.

As of this year, Kooky has supported 106 fan events across 18 countries. This data-driven approach has strengthened the connection between the global K-pop fandom and local markets, underscoring its pivotal role in bridging these communities.

Kooky enhances the autonomy of the fandom ecosystem, acting as a bridge between global networks and local communities to further popularize K-pop in diverse regions. The company highlighted this role as a key factor in its success.

“We are excited to present Kooky’s innovative technology at CES 2025, showcasing how our data-centric approach supports the growth and development of K-pop culture globally,” a company representative said. “We aim to establish new partnerships and expand our network during the event.”

The representative added, “Kooky currently serves users in over 180 countries, with the most active users concentrated in the U.S., Japan, the Philippines, and Singapore. We aim to optimize fan experiences in the U.S., focusing on promising states and launching new events and promotions to strengthen our position in the U.S. and the global K-pop market.”

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
